newsitem.title: USA: USDA to use food stamps to aid N.C. Fran victims.
newsitem.headline: USDA to use food stamps to aid N.C. Fran victims.

text.p: U.S. Agriculture Department said Monday it would use the food stamp program to help victims of Hurricane Fran in North Carolina.
USDA said some current food stamp clients would be allowed to get replacement stamps to restore food lost due to the hurricane, which barrelled through the state late last week, killing 15 people.
It also said it would temporarily waive some program requirements to allow the most severely affected who might not normally be eligible for food stamps to receive help.
USDA will relieve counties of some administrative requirements so more people could be served more effectively.
USDA said specific details about how to apply would announced by the Department of Social Services Tuesday.

"I have toured the affected area and have seen the massive devastation caused by this storm," Agriculture Secretary Dan Glickman said in a statement. "The Clinton administration stands ready to provide assistance to help the citizens of North Carolina rebuild their lives."
